newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to allocate cash for new AN-140 turbo-prop.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to allocate cash for new AN-140 turbo-prop.

text.p: Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko has told the Ukrainian government to allocate three million hryvnias ($1.63 million) to build a first test model of a new Antonov-140 passenger plane, a government official told Reuters on Thursday.

The official said the An-140, which would carry 52 passengers and 4.9 tonnes of cargo, would be completed "in the nearest future". The government earlier this month allocated 1.5 million hryvnias to the project.
The short-haul turbo-prop plane is meant to replace the ageing An-24, popular in the former Soviet Union , Latin America, Africa and China.
Sources in the ministry for machine building, military complex and conversion said the An-140 would cost $6.5 million -- far less than their Western-made equivalents.
The An-140 will be tested by the end of 1997 and experts said $15 million were needed to launch production.
The transport ministry has asked the government to include funds for orders of four An-140s in this year's budget, which could be passed next month, but no decision has been taken yet.

The Antonov design bureau said recently that former Soviet airlines had ordered about 200 An-140s for the next three years, putting total world demand at 600 to 900 planes and domestic demand at 100 planes in the next few years.
Last year Ukraine won a tender in Iran to convert a helicopter plant in the central city of Isfahan into a plane construction plant. Kiev hopes to produce 10 An-140s there a year.
